# Accessibility Instructions

## When this applies
Always, when writing or reviewing UI markup, components, or user-facing content.

## Guidelines
- Use semantic HTML elements (`button`, `nav`, `main`, `label`) instead of generic `div`/`span` with click handlers or ARIA roles bolted on.
- Ensure every interactive element is reachable and operable via keyboard alone (tab order, `Enter`/`Space` activation, visible focus states).
- Provide meaningful text alternatives: `alt` text for informative images, accessible names for icon-only buttons, and associated `<label>`s for form inputs.
- Maintain a minimum color contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text (WCAG AA) and never convey information by color alone.
- Announce dynamic content changes (validation errors, toasts, loading states) using ARIA live regions so screen reader users are notified.

## Anti-patterns
- Using `div onclick` for buttons/links instead of native interactive elements.
- Removing focus outlines (`outline: none`) without providing a visible alternative focus style.
- Images with empty or missing `alt` attributes when the image conveys information.
